name: implications-as-contract-prototypes
claim: Implications are prototypes for contracts: an implication encodes a behavioral invariant at the prompt level, and when code crystallizes around that invariant the implication is elevated to a contract, while implications that can never become contracts (pure reasoning directives, tone guidance) stay implications indefinitely.

evidence.detail: One belief encodes extraction-isolation rules as an implication - behavioral directives surfaced via the prompt. Another encodes state-transition rules as a contract - structural invariants verified by a drift check in code. The difference is not the importance of the rule but whether code exists to enforce it. If a validation module were built to verify extraction output, the implication could be promoted to a contract. The implication is prototyping the invariant at the prompt level until code catches up.

Atomization migration (plans/atomize): claim trimmed to its conclusion per claim discipline (cb:b402); the basis lives in deps. Previous claim: Implications are prototypes for contracts. An implication encodes a behavioral invariant at the prompt level - compliance depends on the agent reading and following it. When code crystallizes around that invariant (a validation module, a state machine, a verify_against_contract/0 implementation), the implication should be elevated to a contract. Contracts provide strict guarantees because code enforces them and tests verify them. Implications that can never become contracts (pure reasoning directives, tone guidance) stay as implications indefinitely. Implications that could become contracts are effectively prototyping the invariant until code catches up.
